chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fadhl from al-Mufaddal ibn Salih from Zayd, Abu Usamah, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the pregnant woman whose husband has died, whether she is entitled to maintenance (nafaqah), and he said, 'No.'
ai.seo_question: Is a pregnant widow entitled to financial maintenance during her waiting period after her husband's death?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that a pregnant widow is not entitled to maintenance (*nafaqah*) during her *iddah* following her husband's death, distinguishing this ruling from the case of divorce. This specific legal nuance is significant in Shia jurisprudence as it highlights the difference between the financial obligations of the husband during life versus the fixed duration of *iddah* after death, where maintenance ceases upon the husband's demise regardless of pregnancy. The ruling underscores the principle that *nafaqah* is tied to the marital bond's active financial responsibility, which concludes with death, while the pregnancy serves primarily to determine the length of the waiting period.
